title: Hasty Well Depth and Drilling Cost
meta_description: Hasty wells have a 160-foot median depth; see local yields, water levels, drilling costs, and risks before buying rural property.
h1: Hasty, Colorado Well Depth, Yield, and Cost Guide
intro_html:
Buying land near Hasty means looking closely at the well record, not relying on a broad regional average. Within 5 miles of Hasty, Colorado, DWR permit records show 148 wells, with 109 recorded as constructed and 111 reporting total depth. The local records point to a median depth of 160 feet, but the spread is wide. Water production also varies, although the available yield records are limited to 18 wells.

This page uses the Hasty-area permit data to help you review a property near McClave, Las Animas, Wiley, Lamar, or Eads. Treat the mapped records as due diligence, not a guarantee for a new hole. A neighboring well can help a driller plan, but the actual result depends on the lot, formation, casing, and completion.

sections.heading: Hasty well depths range well beyond the 160-foot median
sections.html:
The median reported well depth near Hasty is 160 feet. The middle half of wells runs from 36 to 302 feet, so a bid based only on the median can miss the conditions on a particular lot. The 90th-percentile depth is 486 feet, and the deepest recorded well is 600 feet.

Depth records are split across the plains formations: 39% are under 100 feet, 34% fall from 100 to 300 feet, 25% are from 300 to 600 feet, and 2% exceed 600 feet. For a driller's estimate, ask for a base depth and a clear per-foot charge if the hole must continue. Hasty's alluvium and plains sedimentary rock are different from fractured granite, but formation changes can still make depth unpredictable.

sections.heading: Reported Hasty yields are strong, but the sample is small
sections.html:
Only 18 wells in the Hasty records report a pump yield, so the yield statistics deserve caution. Among those reports, the median is 53.0 gallons per minute, with the middle half from 18.8 to 187.5 gallons per minute. The recorded mix shows 78% producing 15 or more gallons per minute, 17% producing 5 to 15, and 6% producing 1 to 5.

No recorded well in this data is under 1 gallon per minute. That is encouraging for a buyer, but it does not promise the same result on an untested parcel. Ask for the neighboring well's completed depth, aquifer, pump test, and recovery information. A domestic well still needs suitable storage, pressure equipment, and water-quality testing even when the reported yield is high.

sections.heading: The Hasty water-level record is too limited for a trend
sections.html:
The local data includes only 1 reported static water level. That record shows water at 145 feet, and the reported median and middle-half values are both 145 feet. With one measurement, there is no meaningful water-level-by-decade series to show a rising or dropping water table.

Do not use the 160-foot median well depth as the expected water depth. A well may continue below the water-bearing zone, and static level can differ from the pumping level. Before buying, request the well construction and permit documents for the specific property and nearby wells. A driller can also explain how the local alluvium or sedimentary aquifer may affect casing, grout, pump setting, and seasonal performance.

sections.heading: Hasty's permit history shows long use, with Hoffman most active
sections.html:
Permit activity near Hasty spans several decades. Records show 3 permits from the 1960s, 14 from the 1970s, 12 from the 1980s, 19 from the 1990s, 43 from the 2000s, 9 from the 2010s, and 3 from the 2020s. The newest permit year in the records is 2023. The use mix is 33% domestic or household, 30% stock, 19% irrigation, and 22% monitoring.

Hoffman, listed as Hoffman, Earl, appears on 30 records. Authorized, listed as Pe, Pg, appears on 19, and S. E. Camp Drilling appears on 7. These names identify activity in the records, not a recommendation or proof of current availability. The aquifer labels include 120 unnamed or fractured-bedrock wells, 13 Dakota wells, and 4 Cheyenne wells, with no Denver Basin aquifer wells recorded.

sections.heading: A median-depth Hasty well models at $11,600 to $20,800 finished
sections.html:
For Hasty's alluvium and plains sedimentary rock, the drilling model uses a typical rate of $35 to $55 per foot. At the 160-foot median depth, the drilled hole models at about $5,600 to $8,800. That is not the full project price.

A finished well including the pump, tank, trenching, and electrical models at about $11,600 to $20,800 at the median depth. A deeper hole, difficult access, different casing or grout requirements, and site-specific electrical or trench work can change the bid. Ask the contractor to separate drilling, casing, grout, pump equipment, pressure tank, trenching, electrical work, testing, and permit-related work. Compare bids on the same scope rather than on the per-foot number alone.

sections.heading: Check water quality, yield, septic, and building limits before closing
sections.html:
Mapped environmental information within about 10 miles includes 3 PFAS sampling or contamination sites, 2 historic mine features, and 1 EPA Superfund or cleanup site. Those mapped locations do not establish that a particular well is contaminated, but they are a reason to order laboratory testing and review the well's location and construction history. Test for the concerns appropriate to the property and intended use.

Low yield and dry holes remain possible even though the recorded yield sample is favorable. Confirm the permit allows the intended household, stock, or irrigation use; exempt household-use wells have a 35-gpm pumping limit, and over-appropriated basins may require an augmentation plan. Before building, confirm the well location works with the septic system, driveway, electrical service, house site, and access for a rig. Local review is important before excavation.

faq.q: How deep are wells near Hasty, Colorado?
faq.a: The median reported depth within 5 miles of Hasty is 160 feet. The middle half runs from 36 to 302 feet, while the 90th percentile is 486 feet and the deepest recorded well is 600 feet. Depth varies by lot and formation, so use nearby construction records to refine a drilling estimate rather than treating 160 feet as a guarantee.

faq.q: How much does it cost to drill a well in Hasty, Colorado?
faq.a: The local drilling model uses $35 to $55 per foot. At the 160-foot median depth, the drilled hole models at about $5,600 to $8,800. A finished well with pump, tank, trenching, and electrical models at about $11,600 to $20,800. A deeper hole or more difficult site can raise the final bid.

faq.q: How much water do Hasty wells produce?
faq.a: Only 18 Hasty-area wells report a pump yield, so the sample is limited. The reported median is 53.0 gallons per minute, with the middle half from 18.8 to 187.5. Records show 78% producing 15 or more gallons per minute and 0% under 1 gallon per minute. Those figures describe recorded wells, not a promise for a new well.

faq.q: Is well water near Hasty, Colorado safe to drink?
faq.a: The permit map cannot establish drinking-water safety. Within about 10 miles are 3 PFAS sampling or contamination sites, 2 historic mine features, and 1 EPA Superfund or cleanup site. A buyer should obtain the well construction record, identify nearby environmental concerns, and have the water tested by a qualified laboratory before using it for household drinking.

faq.q: What should I check before buying land with a well near Hasty?
faq.a: Review the permit, construction depth, aquifer label, pump yield, static water level, and allowed use. The area records include 148 wells, but only 111 report depth, 18 report yield, and 1 reports static water level. Also confirm septic and house-site feasibility, access for drilling equipment, electrical needs, contamination concerns, and any augmentation requirement.
